messages:
marie: audit-bot just flagged a weird pattern — service token 'ml-trainer' made multiple GetObject calls against s3://redwood-prod-training in the past 3h but there is no STS AssumeRole or token mint record in Auth logs. Pausing jobs that reference it now.

ashok: which token id exactly? can you paste the audit entry? cc @taylor (oncall).

marie: entry snippet from CloudTrail (redacted):
```
eventTime: 2025-02-14T08:12:03Z
eventName: GetObject
userIdentity.type: AssumedRole
userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName: ml-trainer-service
requestParameters.bucketName: redwood-prod-training
```
I don't see a corresponding sts:AssumeRole in the same time window in the auth logs.

taylor: acknowledged. I'm revoking the token binding and pausing the trainer deployment. stepping through now.

kat: fwiw KMS logs show decrypts for different key IDs earlier this morning, but none mapped to the bucket KMS key. That could explain the mismatch if objects are stored with a different CMK or uploaded with public ACLs. checking S3 server-access logs.

devops-rosa: I'm applying an immediate bucket policy deny for any access by principal arn:aws:iam::*:role/ml-trainer* and adding a temporary explicit deny for GetObject, PutObject. Command I'm running:
```
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-prod-training --policy '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ml-trainer"},"Action":"s3:*","Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-training","arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-training/*"]}]}'
```
I'll keep the change for now; we can rollback if it breaks batch ingest.

ashok: good. Also check for pre-signed URLs and object ACLs. A compromised build system could have created presigned URLs with long expiry. Search for PutObject with Content-MD5 and x-amz-signature patterns in logs.

marie: found two PutObject events from 2025-02-13 that look like CI artifacts uploaded from the `trainer-ci` service account. They used a different CMK (alias/aws/s3) — objects look public=false. Not sure how ml-trainer got read access.

taylor: possibility: ml-trainer role is being assumed by an internal proxy (infra-service) that has a cross-account role mapping. Searching role-attachment history now. If true, we need to revoke trust policy on that proxy.

kat: enabled CloudTrail data events for S3 + KMS for the bucket and turned on object-level logging to the security log bucket. Also bumped retention for the next 30d.

marie: created an adhoc audit query in Splunk to correlate CloudTrail, KMS, and our AuthN logs — running now.

sec-bot: automatic: incident INC-2025-042 created, severity: high, owners: taylor, marie.

taylor: confirmed — ownership accepted. Immediate action list: 1) Revoke ml-trainer STS tokens / rotate its service credentials; 2) Patch bucket policy (done by rosa); 3) Rotate CMK used by training bucket and re-encrypt objects; 4) Identify any presigned URL issuance; 5) Postmortem in 72h.

devops-rosa: revoked deployment serviceaccount secrets in k8s for trainer namespace and restarted pods. kube command: `kubectl delete secret trainer-service-secret -n trainer-prod` and redeployed with new creds.

ashok: from quick grep, the infra-service added a new role-binding last week that included `sts:AssumeRole` on ml-trainer. tagging @infra-team for why that change rolled without a PR note.

marie: adding temporary alert: if we detect S3 GetObject where CloudTrail principalType==AssumedRole but no matching STS event within +/- 5m, fire pager. This would catch mismatches like this.

kat: reminder: enable object lock/versioning snapshot before CMK rotation so we can avoid data loss.

taylor: good call. we'll snapshot then rotate. I'll also schedule a focused audit: list all roles that have wildcard trusts and flag them.

marie: next steps: keep this channel for updates, will add a quick timeline to the incident ticket. If anyone finds evidence of data exfil, escalate to legal immediately.

ashok: thanks everyone. quick ask: after we finish, can we run a policy lint across role trust policies to detect insecure patterns? esp wide `Principal:\"*\"` or cross-account wildcards.

taylor: yes — adding a task to infra backlog and will include a pre-merge bot check for role-trust diffs.

marie: update 09:20Z: RBAC misconfig appears to be a trust/assume-role escalation introduced by infra-service change on 2025-02-07. We've applied deny and rotated creds; will include mitigations in postmortem.

sec-bot: automatic: incident INC-2025-042 updated: mitigation in place, monitoring enabled.

marie: closing channel for now — if new info surfaces reopen thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
